sources.smoothing: Ported from racing_game terrain_smoothing (radius 2 m, sigma 1, strength 0.35, one pass) as an integer kernel [game]. Weights are round-down(exp(-i^2 / 2) * 1024) = 1024, 621, 138; the exact value for i = 2 is 138.6, so the outer taps are 0.4 of a unit light, far below the 1/256 m height quantum.
sources.crown_and_verge: Crown ridge rounding 0.5 m (the game's sqrt(d^2 + 0.25) - 0.5 form without the square root) and verge drop 0.06 m [game].
sources.blend: Blend widths per highway class are the RoadAttributes::blend_mm defaults the game uses today (src/layer/road_attributes.cpp: 3, 3, 5, 5, 5, 8, 10, 12, 15, 15 m by class rank, a link shares its parent's rank), read at implementation time; test_carve_params compares every entry against resolve_road_attributes. The default entry is [assumed]. The design's illustrative table (primary 10 m, trunk 12 m, ...) was not used, because the design says the table records the game's own values. Within [blend_min_mm, blend_max_mm] = 3 m .. 15 m of PLAN.md 6.3 step 4; blend_slope_factor 3 caps the smooth step's peak slope (2 |dz| / b) at the 1:1.5 cut/fill limit.
sources.deck: Deck clearance 0.55 m, ramp 4 m [game]; the footprint is the paved band plus a 1 m margin [assumed].
sources.junction_fade: Decision D42 (design 4.2, 4.3, 15): inside a junction each approach's paved relief (crown, the sidewalk step of a raise) fades out over clamp(2 * relief / slope, min, max) from its trim line and its verge term (outside the paved band) over verge_mm, so the weights mix the approach bases. slope 10 per mille keeps the fade itself at 0.4 of the usual 25 per mille crossfall [assumed]; min 3 m [assumed]; max 15 m, the blend maximum [assumed]; verge 1.5 m: the 0.06 m verge drop fades at <= 0.08, the verge's own slope order [assumed], and verge_mm <= min_mm keeps the verge weight below the crown weight (the blend stays a convex combination of approach heights).
